{{technical|date=May 2025}}
}}In mathematics, an [[autonomous system (mathematics)|autonomous system]] is a dynamic equation on a [[smooth manifold]]. A '''non-autonomous system''' is a dynamic equation on a smooth [[fiber bundle]] <math>Q\to \mathbb R</math> over <math>\mathbb R</math>. For instance, this is the case of [[non-autonomous mechanics]].

An ''r''-order differential equation on a fiber bundle <math>Q\to \mathbb R</math> is represented by a closed subbundle of a [[jet bundle]] <math>J^rQ</math> of <math>Q\to \mathbb R</math>. A dynamic equation on <math>Q\to \mathbb R</math> is a differential equation which is algebraically solved for a higher-order derivatives.

In particular, a first-order dynamic equation on a fiber bundle <math>Q\to \mathbb R</math> is a kernel of the [[covariant differential]] of some connection <math>\Gamma</math> on <math>Q\to \mathbb R</math>. Given bundle coordinates <math>(t,q^i)</math> on <math>Q</math> and the adapted coordinates <math>(t,q^i,q^i_t)</math> on a first-order jet manifold <math>J^1Q</math>, a first-order dynamic equation reads

: <math>q^i_t=\Gamma (t,q^i).</math>

For instance, this is the case of [[non-autonomous mechanics| Hamiltonian non-autonomous mechanics]].

A second-order dynamic equation

: <math>q^i_{tt}=\xi^i(t,q^j,q^j_t)</math> 

on <math>Q\to\mathbb R</math> is defined as a holonomic
connection <math>\xi</math> on a jet bundle <math>J^1Q\to\mathbb R</math>. This
equation also is represented by a connection on an [[affine bundle|affine]] jet bundle <math>J^1Q\to Q</math>. Due to the canonical
embedding <math>J^1Q\to TQ</math>, it is equivalent to a geodesic equation
on the tangent bundle <math>TQ</math> of <math>Q</math>. A [[free motion equation]] in non-autonomous mechanics exemplifies a second-order non-autonomous dynamic equation.
